Last week, I watched a junior designer spend 45 minutes tweaking a prompt. The result? A generic dark-mode dashboard with glassmorphism cards — the same output every AI tool spits out when you ask for “something modern.”
The problem wasn’t the tool. It was the prompt.
Here’s the truth: 90% of designers write prompts backwards. They start with what they want (“generate a landing page”) and hope the AI fills in the context. That’s like asking a chef to “make something good” without mentioning dietary restrictions, occasion, or budget.
The fix? Start with context. Always.
Press enter or click to view image in full size

The Wrong Way vs. The Right Way
The wrong way (what most people do):
“Generate a landing page for my SaaS.”
Result: Generic dark-mode dashboard. Glassmorphism cards. No clue who your user is. Three hours of fixing later, you wish you’d just designed it yourself.
The right way (what top designers do):
“Generate a landing page for B2B HR managers aged 35–50 who value ROI data over flashy visuals. They need to justify the purchase to a CFO. Include pricing transparency, a calculator, and social proof from Fortune 500 companies. Output as a wireframe with copy suggestions.”
